what: Cards are laid evenly on a sphere in a golden-angle spiral, and the sphere’s angles are folded by .4 and spread into a single front dome — the front card is largest, and cards recede and shrink toward the edges (wide screen dome radius .58w, perspective 2.8w, card .18w). Drag and wheel only change the target angle, and the sphere follows over 1s power2.out (drag follows the hand as far as the front card moves, wheel .1°/px). When it stops, the card closest to the center moves to the center over .9s expo.inOut. Pressing a card rotates it to the center and then fires fx:pick. On first load, cards grow from .5× to full size over 1.2s power3.out (.03s apart).

options.[data-fx-part=card]: Cards to attach to the sphere (children, multiple). If short, they are duplicated up to the fill count (duplicates are aria-hidden and tabindex -1)
options.fill: Number of cards to fill the sphere, default 48
options.fold: Multiplier for folding the sphere angle, default .4 — at 1 it is a true sphere (back cards appear flipped)
options.fx:pick: Event emitted by the clicked card (or the original if it is a clone) after it reaches the center — the consumer goes from here to the detail
options.--fx-card: Card width (css variable) — the part fills it at every width

note: The original draws the cards as WebGL panels and adds a particle formation effect and fluid handprints — this part moves DOM cards with the same DOM projection values. The card count (17 in the original) is duplicated up to 48 to match the on-screen spacing (neighboring card centers about 450px apart, at 1440), and the drag multiplier is a value measured on screen (guess)
